sections.section_title: Initial Presentation and Early Differential Diagnosis
sections.description: Describes the patient's arrival to care, chief complaints, physical examination findings leading physicians toward considering deep‐neck soft tissue disorders versus systemic causes.
subtopics: Adult male ~45 yrs old presents progressively worsening cervical swelling over three weeks
Weakness confined initially to hip flexors accompanied by mild myalgia
Nailfold microscopy shows microhaemorrhages suggesting systemic vasculopathy
Contrast CT‐neck demonstrates diffuse oedema involving strap muscles extending into retropharyngeal space
Primary diagnostics triage centers Ludwig’s angina versus idiopathic angioedema
